newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission urges joint action on energy problems.
newsitem.headline: Commission urges joint action on energy problems.

text.p: The European Commission is expected on Wednesday to call for a more efficient, coordinated effort to tackle the European Union's growing dependence on non-EU energy supplies.
According to a Commission communication, due to be published on Wednesday, the EU's reliance on external supplies of gas, oil and other fuels will soar from 50 to 70 percent by 2010.

At the same time, there is increasing pressure on EU member states to introduce more competitive electricity and gas prices, and at the same time reduce the damage the energy sector does to the environment, calls for a hard-hitting response.

They will only be able effectively to cope with these challenges, the Commission believes, if they adopt common energy policy targets, work together to acheve them and target their efforts more acurately.

To this end, Wednesday's communication details all the energy-related initiatives currently being carried out by the EU and individual member states, ranging from energy-saving schemes and research into clean coal technology to nuclear safety programmes and cooperation schemes with energy-rich countries in Eastern Europe and North Africa.

"Having this clear picture will enable us to see how best we can coordinate actions, (avoid) overlaps and best tackle the problems ahead," a spokesman for EU Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis told Reuters.
